title: Bekovich-Cherkassky Expedition to Khiva
summary: In 1717 Captain Alexander Bekovich-Cherkassky led the first Russian army expedition to Khiva on Peter I's orders. The tsar's written instructions called for forts on the Amu Darya, making the Khivan khan a subject and seeking a route to India. The expedition was destroyed and Bekovich was killed, and the episode became a Russian saying.

uncertainty.note: Russkiy Mir says the detachment set out through the desert in June 1717; the month of its destruction is not taken from an opened page. Preparations and earlier Caspian surveys began earlier.

where.modern_name: Khiva, Uzbekistan (pin is the expedition's destination, a proxy)

importance.justification: First Russian army expedition to Khiva, ending in the loss of the whole force and Peter I's Central Asian plans.

audience_note: Describes the killing and mutilation of a commander and the enslavement of captives.

sources.title: Eastward Motion of Peter the Great's Empire
sources.publisher: RUDN Journal of Russian History (RUDN University)
sources.author: Evgenii V. Anisimov

reviewer_note: Year 1717 rests on Russkiy Mir (a foundation site); RUDN article confirms the aims and the failure but I did not find a destruction month on an opened page. Pin is Khiva as proxy; the actual fight was about 150 km away per Russkiy Mir.
